resumen: El bus no llega y Tom tiene que decidir. Reusa casi todo el vocabulario de la primera.
texto:
Every morning Tom takes the same bus at the same time. He waits at the corner, by the small shop, and the bus comes at seven.

Today the bus did not come.

He waited. He looked at his watch. Ten minutes. Twenty. Some other people were waiting too, and then, one by one, they went away.

“It's not coming,” said a woman. “There's no bus today.”

Tom did not know what to do. Work was far. If he waited more, he would be late; if he walked, he would also be late, but he would get there.

So he walked.

It took him fifty minutes. On the way he saw things he had never seen before: a red door, a very old tree, a man who gives bread to the birds every day.

He got to work late. Nobody said anything.

“How was your morning?” said Ana.

Tom thought about it for a moment.

“Good,” he said. “It was good.”

every.nota: «every day» = todos los días. Va con verbo en singular: «every day is…»

same.nota: casi siempre lleva «the» delante: the same bus

watch.nota: también el verbo «mirar/ver»: watch a movie

too.nota: al final de la frase es «también»; delante de un adjetivo es «demasiado»

never.nota: ya es negativo: «I never saw it», no «I didn't never»

anything.nota: en frase negativa es «nada»: «nobody said anything» = nadie dijo nada

get to.nota: «he got to work» = llegó al trabajo. Con «home» no lleva «to»

sentidos.take: tardar, tomar (tiempo) — «it took him fifty minutes» = le tomó cincuenta minutos
sentidos.so: así que — acá conecta la decisión con lo que hizo
sentidos.there: allí — «he would get there» = llegaría allá
